The e+e− → π+π− channel contributes approximately 70% to the leading order hadronic vacuum polarization term a_had,LO in the muon g−2 calculation.
CMD-3 measured the e+e− → π+π− cross section in the energy range 0.3 < s < 1.2 GeV with high precision.
CMD-3 results are in significant tension with BaBar and KLOE ISR measurements of the same cross section.
The joint fit of all π+π− data yields a χ2/dof = 2.18, indicating poor compatibility between datasets.
The Particle Data Group (PDG) prescription was applied to scale experimental uncertainties by the factor √(χ2/dof) = 2.18 to accommodate tensions.
The combined fit including CMD-3 data gives a_had,LO(e+e−) = (696.2 ± 2.9) × 10^−10.
Previous dispersive method estimates of a_had,LO(e+e−) were around (693.1 ± 4.0) × 10^−10.
The Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment including CMD-3 data is a_SM = (11,659,184 ± 4) × 10^−10.
The experimental world average for the muon anomalous magnetic moment is a_exp = (11,659,205.9 ± 2.2) × 10^−10.
The discrepancy between a_SM and a_exp is about 4.7σ when including CMD-3 data.
Excluding CMD-3 data reduces a_had,LO to (694.0 ± 2.0 ± 1.4 ± 0.4) × 10^−10 and increases the discrepancy to about 5σ.
Using CMD-3 data alone for π+π− yields a_had,LO = (723.4 ± 3.1 ± 3.1 ± 3.5) × 10^−10, consistent with experiment at ~1σ.
The authors used a model-independent piecewise linear parameterization for the cross section.
Uncertainties in a_had,LO arise from experimental errors, parameterization systematics, and radiative corrections.
Other hadronic channels were included with similar treatment to build the total hadronic contribution to muon g−2.
The CMD-3 data tension with BaBar and KLOE dominates the poor fit quality in the 0.6 < s < 1.0 GeV region.
The PDG scaling method is debated but widely used to handle incompatible measurements.
The authors confirm CMD-3's observation that their data alone imply a_SM consistent with a_exp within ~1σ.
The total hadronic leading order contribution from all channels is estimated as (696.2 ± 2.9) × 10^−10.
The CMD-3 measurement was performed at the VEPP-2000 collider using the CMD-3 detector.
